title: Field Accelerator: Demo Arc + Positioning Workshop
topics: Positioning Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private
Live demo run-through with failure scenarios
summary: Internal enablement session focused on tightening the demo storyline (the demo arc), rehearsing answers to cost/latency/security objections, and practicing quick recovery when a demo path breaks. SEs practiced a 7-minute core demo with variant hooks for Retail and FinServ buyers. Team agreed on a 3-bullet battlecard for each objection and to record two short clips for self-study.
action_items: Samir Patel | Produce 3-bullet objection battlecards (latency, cost, on-prem) | 2025-08-18
Maya Chen | Record 2 demo clips (core 7-min, and graceful-fallback flow) and upload to enablement repo | 2025-08-20
Jordan Blake | Draft 3 customer questions for Retail buyer persona and send to group | 2025-08-15
Liam O'Connor | Update one-pager on Dedicated pricing examples (add regional latency notes) | 2025-08-22
next_steps: Samir to share updated slide deck with simplified demo arc
Schedule follow-up 30-min run on 2025-08-25 for recording feedback
Push demo clips to LMS and tag for quick review prior to Q4 field kickoff
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel (AE): Alright folks, kickin' off at 2pm. Thanks for making time, this is the Field Accelerator — want to boil down the demo arc to something repeatable for next week's roadshows.
[00:12] Jordan Blake (Field SE): Hey Samir, quick note — I'll be out demoing in EMEA next month so anything we lock now would be great.
[00:19] Maya Chen (SE): Cool, I'll lead the demo portion. Goal is a 7-minute core flow and two 60s hooks for retail/finserv.
[00:27] Priya Rao (AE): Also, have to make sure we hit the security checklist early — customers ask about KMS, audit logs, SOC2.
[00:34] Liam O'Connor: Yup, short security plug at the top, then problem, then live.
[00:40] Samir: Sound good. Maya, take us through the arc.
[00:44] Maya: Sure, so step one is 'context & pain' 60s: show perf slide — 99th p99 latency at typical seq length, and call out cost per 1k tokens.
[00:55] Maya: step two is 'live problem' — call our hosted API, show prompt engineering, switch to Dedicated for predictable throughput, then show fallback to Private for regulated data.
[01:07] Jordan: Just flag — customers sometimes conflate Dedicated and Private; they want an on-prem box. We should be explicit.
[01:15] Maya: Good point, I'll add a one-liner: Dedicated = reserved GPU pool managed by Redwood; Private = customer-managed VPC / on-prem.
[01:24] Priya: How do we handle the latency vs cost pushback? They ask 'why not just use OpenAI, it's cheaper' all the time.
[01:32] Samir: Prep the reframes: 1) predictable unit cost at scale, 2) routing/fallback keeps app online during outages, 3) observability — token-level cost breakdowns.
[01:42] Maya: And show a quick chart — effective cost per 1M tokens after batching/caching. But small customers see sticker shock up front.
[01:50] Aisha Gomez: can we show a real example — like a retail site with burst traffic Black Friday? Numbers land better.
[01:58] Maya: I'll prepare a Black Friday scenario slide.
[02:03] [02:03] Maya: Live demo start — opening the Redwood Console. // slight stutter in audio //
[02:15] Speaker 4: (inaudible)
[02:18] Maya: Ok, I'm doing a gen call — prompt: 'Summarize customer reviews for product X and extract sentiment' — results streaming.
[02:30] Maya: Note the stream latency, you can see tokens come in every 200ms. // transcription might show 0.2 sec but network varies
[02:41] Jordan: If the customer asks about KV cash — I always have to correct to KV cache.
[02:47] Samir: (laughs) classic.
[02:50] Maya: Now I'll switch routing policy — route heavier requests to Dedicated pool.
[02:59] Maya: Switching... small pause — live effect shows stable throughput.
[03:08] Priya: If the Dedicated is full will requests fail? We need to explain burst policy.
[03:15] Maya: We show autoscale + burst to shared capacity and, if necessary, fallback to hosted model variant. Essentially graceful degradation.
[03:25] Jordan: Customers wanna know about data retention and encryption — where does the data live for Hosted?
[03:30] Samir: Hosted keeps ephemeral logs by default; we have options for retention and KMS integration. Mention SOC2 and optional HSM for Private.
[03:40] Maya: (slight mis-transcribe) "We also offer audit trails in the console for token-level tracing" — that's a good soundbite.
[03:50] Liam: Roleplay time — Samir, you're the skeptical buyer, Priya you're buyer persona retail.
[03:58] Samir (AE as buyer): So why shouldn't I just run an open model on my cloud VMs and avoid vendor lock?
[04:06] Priya (Retail buyer): Yeah, and what about raw latency? I can't have pages waiting.
[04:12] Maya (SE): Good Qs — Rebuttal framework: 1) TCO includes ops and kernel optimizations — our runtime reduces per-token cost via batching and KV caching, 2) Predictable latency with Dedicated pools + SLA, 3) We can deploy Private for control.
[04:30] Samir: Say that in two sentences.
[04:33] Maya: Short: "You can build yourself but you pay heavy ops tax; Redwood gives a pre-tuned runtime, predictable pricing at scale, and options for private deployment when you need it."
[04:45] Jordan: Customer interruption — what about regulatory regions? Do we have data residency?
[04:50] Maya: Yes — we can region-pin and offer VPC/on-prem; mention audit logs and KMS.
[04:56] [05:00] Maya: Now we'll run a failure scenario — simulate Dedicated pool exhaustion and show fallback to hosted variant. // pause //
[05:12] Maya: Triggering load — requests start queueing, console shows autoscale behavior, fallback kicks in to compatible model variant with slightly higher lat, but keeps app responsive.
[05:28] Priya: Great — make sure we call out the exact numbers: e.g., 10% latency increase but 40% cost saving vs full redundancy.
[05:38] Aisha: Can we quantify ops time saved? Decision makers care about staff costs.
[05:43] Liam: We'll use the customer benchmark sheet we shared last week — cite 2 FTE equivalent saved per 100M tokens.
[05:52] Samir: Objection handling — common lines: "Your solution is expensive", "We need on-prem", "We already have embeddings provider". Let's rapid-fire rebuttals.
[06:03] Maya: For "expensive": show batching, caching, and quant recommendation — show Optimize toolkit. For "on-prem": private offering + managed control plane. For "embeddings": we support multiple embedding formats and can ingest existing vectors.
[06:18] Jordan: Can we get a one-liner for each? Field reps need 10-12 word answers.
[06:25] Maya: I'll craft those. Example: "Expensive? Our batching & caching reduces per-token cost by X; we tune to your profile."
[06:35] Samir: Let's do a timed run — Jordan, you're demoing the retail flow; Priya as buyer interrupts after 90s with the 'why is this better than OpenAI' script.
[06:44] Jordan: Starting now. [06:46] Jordan: Opening product catalog, prompt to summarize 1k reviews — streaming results. [07:05] Priya: (interrupt) Why not call OpenAI?
[07:09] Jordan: Reframe: At scale you need predictable capacity, observability, and routing policies — OpenAI doesn't give you a dedicated GPU pool or private rollback.
[07:20] Priya: Customer asks about guarantees—SLAs?
[07:24] Jordan: We have SLA tiers on Dedicated; explain support and incident runbook.
[07:31] Samir: Nice. Quick feedback: tighten language, avoid deep infra detail unless buyer asks.
[07:38] Maya: Now demo the Optimize suggestions — show recommended quant profile and cost delta.
[07:46] Maya: The console suggests int8 quant and batching for this workload — shows 2.3x cost reduction on the projection.
[07:56] Aisha: Will quant affect quality?
[07:59] Maya: Slightly for some generative tasks; we recommend evals and holdout prompt sets. This is where the evals and regression alerts matter.
[08:10] [08:10] (audio glitch)
[08:13] Samir: Okay, meta — let's capture the 3 bullets each rep should memorize: value prop, fallback story, and security plug.
[08:23] Priya: Value prop: predictable performance + cost controls. Fallback: autoscale -> fallback model variant -> private option. Security plug: SOC2, KMS, audit logs.
[08:33] Jordan: Can we get pre-made snippets for recorded pitch? 10s/20s/40s.
[08:39] Liam: Yes, Maya will record two clips: quick intro and fallback narrative.
[08:45] Maya: Quick improv: "Redwood gives you pre-tuned inference, predictable pricing, and a private deployment path when regulations demand it."
[08:56] Jordan: Ok, I noticed when the demo switched routing the transcripts had a short dropout — do we practice handling that live?
[09:03] Maya: Yes — script: acknowledge pause, say 'we're switching to dedicated for steady throughput, you'll see a momentary buffer' — keep buyer calm.
[09:13] Priya: Also include line about integrations — SSO/SAML, RBAC.
[09:18] Maya: Noted.
[09:20] [09:20] Roleplay round two — Priya as skeptical CIO.
[09:25] Priya: I worry about compliance — how do you prove data control?
[09:29] Maya: Answer: Private option with HSM/KMS + dedicated audit logs. For hosted, optional retention policies and encryption at rest.
[09:37] Priya: How about model updates and rollback?
[09:39] Maya: We manage model versions and rollouts — can canary and auto-fallback.
[09:44] Samir: Small note — avoid saying 'we handle everything' — say 'we provide the controls and ops tooling to reduce your burden'.
[09:52] Jordan: Quick tech-deep question: how do you handle KV cache across replicas?
[09:57] Maya: (paraphrase) KV cache is sharded and synchronized with the runtime; it's in-memory per worker with overflow handling, not persisted across cold starts — best phrased simply for field: "fast in-memory cache reduces repeated prompt cost."
[10:14] Aisha: Can that be misheard as "KV cash"? People will laugh.
[10:18] (laughter)
[10:22] Samir: Alright last segment: recording plan and distribution.
[10:25] Liam: We'll make two short clips: core 7-min demo trimmed to 5 highlights and a 90s fallback narrative. Add captions for quick scanning.
[10:34] Maya: I'll include callouts for exact phrasing and put timestamps in the deck.
[10:40] Samir: Final recap — action items we captured in the doc. Anything else?
[10:46] Priya: Please include one-liners pinned in Salesforce so AE's see them in the activity bar.
[10:51] Samir: Good call. Liam, can you add that?
[10:55] Liam: Yep.
[10:58] Samir: Ok thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.
[11:02] [11:02] End of recording.
